subject: Post-demo follow-up: Vela reliability comparison & next test plan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@velasystems.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: Vela reliability comparison & next test plan

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we heard today
- Primary concern: predictable availability during peak batch processing windows (120–180 req/s) and graceful degradation when a regional pool is degraded.
- Vela will run a parallel evaluation vs your incumbent hyperscaler endpoints and a managed inference API you evaluated earlier. You're focused on uptime, rate-limit behavior under burst, and how error budgets translate into visible client-side latencies.

Redwood differentiators (short)
- Consistent SLOs across hosted/dedicated/private — same routing and fallback logic so failovers look identical in production.
- Automatic KV/prefix caching reduces burst load without changing client code.
- Transparent per-token cost + latency breakdown per request (helps correlate cost vs error budget usage).

Proposed tests (attached matrix)
1) Controlled burst: ramp 10 -> 200 req/s over 30s, hold 2m, observe 5 minute recovery window. Measure 99th latency, 5xx rate, connection drops. (Owner: Camila)
2) Region failover: inject 30% node loss in primary region and observe cross-region routing/fallback and cache warm-up penalty. (Owner: Priyom)
3) Rate-limit behavior: send concurrent long-context streams to validate graceful backpressure and client-side retry guidance. (Owner: Sean)

Immediate asks
- Can Vela share the hyperscaler endpoint configs you want us to hit (hostnames/keys) and the incumbent throughput profile?
- Can we get two eng contacts who can accept short maintenance windows for failover testing?

Attachments: 20270601-vela-test-matrix.xlsx, sla-compare-hyperscalers.pdf

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30m sync for Wednesday to kick off the test cadence unless you prefer asynchronous coordination.

Sean
Sean Gallagher | Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@velasystems.com>

Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: Vela reliability comparison & next test plan

Sean —

Appreciate the clear summary. We like the proposed tests. A few quick clarifications from the engineering side: 
- For the controlled burst, our incumbent uses token-bucket rate limiting configured at 250 rps per region; we can provide endpoint + key for a test-only key.
- For region failover, we can open a maintenance window Wednesday 06/02 22:00–23:30 PT and give you two hosts in our staging region to run against.
- On rate-limits: our concern is that long-running streams will silently fail and clients won't get a clear 429 vs connection drop. If Redwood can characterize those failure modes (and provide suggested client-side retry windows), that will be helpful.

I'll attach the endpoint inventory to a follow-up note — sending to your email now.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Park | Director, Platform Engineering | Vela Systems
alyssa.park@velasystems.com

Thanks for the window. I’ll own the Controlled Burst test. My plan: 
- Create a k6 script that simulates your client-side mix (short prompts vs 2–4k-token streaming sessions).
- Run 3 iterations during the window (baseline, 2x burst, 4x burst) and capture 50/95/99 latencies, 5xx/4xx breakdown, and connection-level stats.
- I’ll also enable Redwood’s prefix caching for one iteration to show delta in upstream load.

Data we need from you: the ephemeral test key + a sample client payload (headers/content-length) so we can replicate the client behavior exactly.

Alyssa / team —

I’ll lead the Region Failover test during your maintenance window. Quick notes on measurement and rollback: 
- Failure injection approach: we’ll cordon 30% of GPUs in the primary pool (simulated) and observe our smart routing move traffic to the standby region. We’ll measure the additional cold-start penalty (ms) on the first 500 requests and the steady-state 99th over 10 minutes.
- Failback: after 10 minutes we’ll reintroduce nodes and monitor K/V cache warm-up. We expect a measurable but acceptable transient increase in tail latency (~200–500ms) depending on model context length; we’ll capture traces.
- Rollback plan: if error rate > 2% sustained for 5 minutes, we’ll pause and revert routing; we’ll notify you via the eng alias and your on-call.

I’ll post the exact runbook and a short checklist to the shared Drive by EOD.

Priyom
Priyom Das | Reliability Engineering | Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks for the quick turn. A couple of housekeeping items before we run: 
- Please confirm the test-only API key + the hyperscaler endpoint list by EOD tomorrow so Camila can bake the client profile into the scripts.
- If Vela has any DoS protection or WAF that might silently mutate requests (strip headers or inject redirects) please point us to the config owner now so we can coordinate.
- We’ll push a short summary of measured SLOs vs your incumbent and the hyperscaler after the runs — plan to include: uptime, 99th latency, 5xx rate, cold-start penalty, and a short cost delta per 1M tokens.

If that all looks good I’ll lock the calendar invite for the maintenance window and we’ll proceed.
